notes.official:
*hôy* opens a woe-oracle (10:1–4) against those who write unjust law; it is rendered "Woe" under the wave ruling (`hoy-woe-isaiah`), as in the woe-series of 5:8–22, and many commentators take 10:1–4 as the lost seventh woe of that series (Wildberger, *Isaiah 1–12*; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19).

*ḥiqqᵉqê-ʾāwen* "decrees of iniquity" is rendered adjectivally, "iniquitous decrees" (ASV "unrighteous decrees"); *ʾāwen* is "iniquity" at its other Isaiah sites. *ʿāmāl* is "trouble, mischief" (BDB), and the line gives "mischief" in place of ASV "perverseness", which is not a sense of the noun; NRSV paraphrases "oppressive statutes". The Piel participle *mᵉḵattᵉḇîm* with the Piel perfect *kittēḇû* describes scribes who keep producing such texts: the oracle is aimed at written law.

paragraphs.text: לְהַטּ֤וֹת מִדִּין֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְלִגְזֹ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיֵּ֣י עַמִּ֑י לִהְי֤וֹת אַלְמָנוֹת֙ שְׁלָלָ֔ם וְאֶת־יְתוֹמִ֖ים יָבֹֽזּוּ׃

i18n.en: to turn aside the needy from justice, and to rob the poor of my people of their right, that widows may be their spoil, and that they may plunder the fatherless!
i18n.he: לְהַטּ֤וֹת מִדִּין֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְלִגְזֹ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיֵּ֣י עַמִּ֑י לִהְי֤וֹת אַלְמָנוֹת֙ שְׁלָלָ֔ם וְאֶת־יְתוֹמִ֖ים יָבֹֽזּוּ׃

notes.official: *šᵉlālām* "their spoil" and *yāḇōzzû* "they plunder" are the two roots of the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz (8:1, 3), and they recur together at 10:6 ("to take spoil and to seize plunder"). The chapter keeps one English pair for them, "spoil" for *šālāl* and "plunder" for *bzz/baz*, so the echo of the sign-name stays visible.

paragraphs.text: וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם פְּקֻדָּ֔ה וּלְשׁוֹאָ֖ה מִמֶּרְחָ֣ק תָּב֑וֹא עַל־מִי֙ תָּנ֣וּסוּ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה וְאָ֥נָה תַעַזְב֖וּ כְּבוֹדְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And what will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation that shall come from afar? To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory?
i18n.he: וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם פְּקֻדָּ֔ה וּלְשׁוֹאָ֖ה מִמֶּרְחָ֣ק תָּב֑וֹא עַל־מִי֙ תָּנ֣וּסוּ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה וְאָ֥נָה תַעַזְב֖וּ כְּבוֹדְכֶֽם׃

notes.official:
*yôm pᵉquddāh* is rendered "the day of visitation" (ASV). The root *pqd* means attention paid to someone for good or ill, and here the context makes it a day of reckoning (NRSV "the day of punishment"). At 10:12 the finite verb *ʾep̄qōḏ ʿal* takes its ordinary prepositional sense, "I will punish". *šôʾāh* is "desolation" (ASV); NRSV has "calamity".

*kᵉḇôḏᵉḵem* "your glory" follows the wave's strict rule that *kāḇôḏ* is always "glory" (also 10:16, 18). Here the word means the weight of wealth and standing the oppressors have amassed, and NRSV renders it "wealth".

paragraphs.text: בִּלְתִּ֤י כָרַע֙ תַּ֣חַת אַסִּ֔יר וְתַ֥חַת הֲרוּגִ֖ים יִפֹּ֑לוּ בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Nothing remains but to crouch under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
i18n.he: בִּלְתִּ֤י כָרַע֙ תַּ֣חַת אַסִּ֔יר וְתַ֥חַת הֲרוּגִ֖ים יִפֹּ֑לוּ בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*biltî kāraʿ taḥaṯ ʾassîr wᵉṯaḥaṯ hărûḡîm yippōlû* is a crux. *biltî* is "except, nothing but" (BDB), so the first clause is "nothing (remains) but …". The verb *kāraʿ* "crouch, bow down" is singular and *yippōlû* "they fall" is plural, The line renders the first verb as an infinitive ("Nothing remains but to crouch … and they shall fall"), as JPS 1917 does ("They can do nought except crouch"). This smooths over the singular of *kāraʿ*, so the number shift is visible only in the Hebrew. NJPS instead continues the question of 10:3 into 10:4a ("From collapsing under [fellow] prisoners"). ASV has "They shall only bow down …". *taḥaṯ* is rendered "under", its basic sense, picturing bodies beneath the captives and the slain; "among" (NRSV) is the common alternative.

A nineteenth-century conjecture associated with P. de Lagarde redivides the consonants as the divine names Beltis and Osiris ("Beltis crouches, Osiris is shattered"). It is reported in the critical commentaries but not verified here against Lagarde's text. It is not the Masoretic Text and is not adopted (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

The refrain that closes the verse is the fixed wording of `bekhol-zot-lo-shav-appo-refrain-isaiah` (5:25; Heb. 9:11, 16, 20). Its fourth occurrence here ties the woe-oracle to the poem of 9:7–20.

paragraphs.text: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑י וּמַטֶּה־ה֥וּא בְיָדָ֖ם זַעְמִֽי׃

i18n.en: Woe, Assyria, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!
i18n.he: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑י וּמַטֶּה־ה֥וּא בְיָדָ֖ם זַעְמִֽי׃

notes.official:
*hôy ʾaššûr* is a vocative, "Woe, Assyria" (`hoy-woe-isaiah`; compare "Woe, Ariel", 29:1). ASV has "Ho Assyrian". The line keeps the country name, as at 14:25. The masculine pronouns that follow refer to Assyria personified as its king.

*šēḇeṭ* is rendered "rod" and *maṭṭeh* "staff" throughout the chapter (10:5, 15, 24, 26), as at 9:3. The second half, literally "and a staff it (is) in their hand, my indignation", is construed with ASV, "the staff in whose hand is my indignation". NRSV has "the club in their hands is my fury", and many commentators delete *hûʾ bᵉyāḏām* as a gloss. The line translates the Masoretic Text. The image is plain: Assyria is the instrument of YHWH's anger.

paragraphs.text: בְּג֤וֹי חָנֵף֙ אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ וְעַל־עַ֥ם עֶבְרָתִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֔ז ולשימו [וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ] מִרְמָ֖ס כְּחֹ֥מֶר חוּצֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: I will send him against a godless nation, and against the people of my wrath I will give him a charge, to take spoil and to seize plunder, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
i18n.he: בְּג֤וֹי חָנֵף֙ אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ וְעַל־עַ֥ם עֶבְרָתִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֔ז ולשימו [וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ] מִרְמָ֖ס כְּחֹ֥מֶר חוּצֽוֹת׃

notes.official:
*gôy ḥānēp̄* is "a godless nation" (NRSV) under the wave ruling for *ḥānēp̄* (9:16; 10:6), matching the stable 32:6 "godlessness". ASV has "a profane nation". The overlay entry `chanef-broken-everlasting-covenant-isaiah-24` governs the verb at 24:5 and is not extended here.

The ketiv reads ולשימו and the qere וּלְשׂוּמוֹ *ûlᵉśûmô* "and to make him/it". The qere is translated, and the difference does not change the sense. Literally the phrase is "to make it a trampling (*mirmās*) like the mire of the streets"; ASV's "to tread them down" is kept, with the people of the previous clause as the referent.

paragraphs.text: וְהוּא֙ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יְדַמֶּ֔ה וּלְבָב֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יַחְשֹׁ֑ב כִּ֚י לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד בִּלְבָב֔וֹ וּלְהַכְרִ֥ית גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א מְעָֽט׃

i18n.en: Yet he does not so intend, nor does his heart so think; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off nations not a few.
i18n.he: וְהוּא֙ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יְדַמֶּ֔ה וּלְבָב֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יַחְשֹׁ֑ב כִּ֚י לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד בִּלְבָב֔וֹ וּלְהַכְרִ֥ית גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א מְעָֽט׃

paragraphs.text: כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א שָׂרַ֛י יַחְדָּ֖ו מְלָכִֽים׃

i18n.en: For he says: Are not my princes all of them kings?
i18n.he: כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א שָׂרַ֛י יַחְדָּ֖ו מְלָכִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: הֲלֹ֥א כְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ כַּלְנ֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֤א כְאַרְפַּד֙ חֲמָ֔ת אִם־לֹ֥א כְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
i18n.he: הֲלֹ֥א כְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ כַּלְנ֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֤א כְאַרְפַּד֙ חֲמָ֔ת אִם־לֹ֥א כְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

notes.official: The king's boast lists Syrian and Israelite cities taken by Assyria in the later eighth century BCE (Arpad about 740, Damascus 732, Samaria 722/720, Carchemish 717). The three pairs move south toward Judah: Calno and Carchemish, Hamath and Arpad, Samaria and Damascus. The names take their ASV spellings under `march-itinerary-toponyms-isaiah-10`. The verse identifies no site beyond the Hebrew names.

paragraphs.text: כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ מָצְאָ֣ה יָדִ֔י לְמַמְלְכֹ֖ת הָאֱלִ֑יל וּפְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּמִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: As my hand has found the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria,
i18n.he: כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ מָצְאָ֣ה יָדִ֔י לְמַמְלְכֹ֖ת הָאֱלִ֑יל וּפְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּמִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃

notes.official: *hāʾĕlîl* is singular with the article, a collective "the idols" (ASV, JPS 1917; central `elilim-idols-cross-corpus`, which fixes "idols" for *ʾĕlîlîm*). NJPS reads *ʾĕlîl* in its sense "worthless" and renders "the insignificant kingdoms". *pᵉsîlêhem* "their carved images" follows central `pesel-utemunah-…`. The comparative *mi-* ("more than Jerusalem and Samaria") is rendered "exceeded those of" with ASV.

paragraphs.text: הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי לְשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וְלֶאֱלִילֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְלַעֲצַבֶּֽיהָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her images?
i18n.he: הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי לְשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וְלֶאֱלִילֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְלַעֲצַבֶּֽיהָ׃ (ס)

notes.official: Two different nouns stand in parallel: *ʾĕlîlêhā* "her idols" (`elilim-idols-cross-corpus`) and *ʿăṣabbêhā*, from *ʿāṣāḇ* "idol, image" (BDB). The draft and ASV render both "idols". The line now gives *ʿăṣabbîm* "images" (with NRSV), so that the two Hebrew words stay distinct in English. The noun *ʿōṣeḇ* of 48:5 ("my idol") is a separate form, and its rendering is unaffected.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ בְּהַ֥ר צִיּ֖וֹן וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶפְקֹ֗ד עַל־פְּרִי־גֹ֙דֶל֙ לְבַ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֔וּר וְעַל־תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת ר֥וּם עֵינָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass, when the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, that I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the boasting of his haughty looks.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ בְּהַ֥ר צִיּ֖וֹן וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶפְקֹ֗ד עַל־פְּרִי־גֹ֙דֶל֙ לְבַ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֔וּר וְעַל־תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת ר֥וּם עֵינָֽיו׃

notes.official:
*tip̄ʾereṯ rûm ʿênāyw* is rendered "the boasting of his haughty looks". This departs from the wave default "honor" for *tip̄ʾereṯ* (4:2), and the departure is recorded in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10` and the wave-i3-ch10 overlay diff. Here the noun is pejorative, "vaunting, pomp", the arrogance on display in the king's eyes. The Hithpael of the same root follows at 10:15, *hă-yiṯpāʾēr* "shall the axe boast itself", and "boasting" keeps the two words visibly related. ASV has "the glory of his high looks", NRSV "his haughty pride".

*ʾep̄qōḏ* "I will punish" is first person in the Masoretic Text, although the clause's subject is "the Lord" (*ʾăḏōnāy*, `adonai-standalone-title-isaiah`). NRSV reads the third person, "he will punish", with the LXX and Syriac (versional evidence not verified here). The line translates MT, and the shift into divine speech is left as it stands (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר בְּכֹ֤חַ יָדִי֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִ֖י כִּ֣י נְבֻנ֑וֹתִי וְאָסִ֣יר ׀ גְּבוּלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֗ים ועתידתיהם [וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙] שׁוֹשֵׂ֔תִי וְאוֹרִ֥יד כַּאבִּ֖יר יוֹשְׁבִֽים׃

i18n.en: For he has said: By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding; and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have plundered their treasures, and like a valiant man I have brought down those who sit on thrones.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר בְּכֹ֤חַ יָדִי֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִ֖י כִּ֣י נְבֻנ֑וֹתִי וְאָסִ֣יר ׀ גְּבוּלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֗ים ועתידתיהם [וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙] שׁוֹשֵׂ֔תִי וְאוֹרִ֥יד כַּאבִּ֖יר יוֹשְׁבִֽים׃

notes.official:
The ketiv reads ועתידתיהם (*ʿăṯîḏôṯêhem* "their things to come") and the qere וַעֲתוּדוֹתֵיהֶם (*waʿăṯûḏôṯêhem* "their stores, treasures"). The qere is translated.

*kᵉʾabbîr* is rendered "like a valiant man" (ASV). *ʾabbîr* is "mighty, valiant" and is also used of bulls (Ps 22:13; 50:13), which gives NRSV's "like a bull". *yôšᵉḇîm* is the ordinary "inhabitants" or "those who sit". With ASV and NRSV, the line supplies "on thrones", reading *yšb* in its royal sense ("to sit enthroned"); "I have brought down the inhabitants" is the alternative.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּמְצָ֨א כַקֵּ֤ן ׀ יָדִי֙ לְחֵ֣יל הָֽעַמִּ֔ים וְכֶאֱסֹף֙ בֵּיצִ֣ים עֲזֻב֔וֹת כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲנִ֣י אָסָ֑פְתִּי וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ נֹדֵ֣ד כָּנָ֔ף וּפֹצֶ֥ה פֶ֖ה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And my hand has found, like a nest, the riches of the peoples; and as one gathers eggs that are forsaken, I have gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or chirped.
i18n.he: וַתִּמְצָ֨א כַקֵּ֤ן ׀ יָדִי֙ לְחֵ֣יל הָֽעַמִּ֔ים וְכֶאֱסֹף֙ בֵּיצִ֣ים עֲזֻב֔וֹת כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲנִ֣י אָסָ֑פְתִּי וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ נֹדֵ֣ד כָּנָ֔ף וּפֹצֶ֥ה פֶ֖ה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף׃

notes.official: The king's boast uses a bird-nest image: his hand finds the wealth of the peoples as one finds a nest and gathers abandoned eggs, and no bird flaps a wing or chirps. *kol-hāʾāreṣ* "all the earth" is rendered in its universal scope under `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24` (as extended in wave I-1 to Isaiah's whole-world idiom). Here the scope is the king's own claim to world dominion, not territorial *ʾereṣ* "land".

paragraphs.text: הֲיִתְפָּאֵר֙ הַגַּרְזֶ֔ן עַ֖ל הַחֹצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּ֤ל הַמַּשּׂוֹר֙ עַל־מְנִיפ֔וֹ כְּהָנִ֥יף שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ וְאֶת־מְרִימָ֔יו כְּהָרִ֥ים מַטֶּ֖ה לֹא־עֵֽץ׃

i18n.en: Shall the axe boast itself against the one who hews with it? Shall the saw magnify itself against the one who wields it? As if a rod should wield those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up one who is not wood!
i18n.he: הֲיִתְפָּאֵר֙ הַגַּרְזֶ֔ן עַ֖ל הַחֹצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּ֤ל הַמַּשּׂוֹר֙ עַל־מְנִיפ֔וֹ כְּהָנִ֥יף שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ וְאֶת־מְרִימָ֔יו כְּהָרִ֥ים מַטֶּ֖ה לֹא־עֵֽץ׃

notes.official: The axe-and-saw argument turns 10:5 against itself. The instrument cannot boast against the one who wields it (*yiṯpāʾēr*, Hithpael of *pʾr*, the root of 10:12 "boasting"). *šēḇeṭ* "rod" and *maṭṭeh* "staff" carry the chapter's fixed pair. *lōʾ-ʿēṣ* "not wood" is the one who wields the staff, a person, not timber. ASV has "as if a staff should lift up him that is not wood".

paragraphs.text: לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּמִשְׁמַנָּ֖יו רָז֑וֹן וְתַ֧חַת כְּבֹד֛וֹ יֵקַ֥ד יְקֹ֖ד כִּיק֥וֹד אֵֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: Therefore the Sovereign, YHWH of hosts, will send leanness among his fat ones; and under his glory a burning shall be kindled, like the burning of fire.
i18n.he: לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּמִשְׁמַנָּ֖יו רָז֑וֹן וְתַ֧חַת כְּבֹד֛וֹ יֵקַ֥ד יְקֹ֖ד כִּיק֥וֹד אֵֽשׁ׃

notes.official:
*hā-ʾāḏôn* with the article, before *YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ*, is rendered provisionally "the Sovereign", under `ha-adon-articular-title-isaiah` (wave I-1 decision 1, option B, pending founder ruling). The articular title is distinct from the bare *ʾăḏōnāy* "the Lord" of 10:12. If the founder rules option A, the line reverts to "the Lord, YHWH of hosts" (ASV).

*bᵉmišmannāyw rāzôn* is "leanness among his fat ones" (ASV, literal). NRSV reads *mišmannîm* as "stout warriors" and *rāzôn* as "wasting sickness". *kᵉḇōḏô* "his glory" (the Assyrian king's) follows the strict "glory" rule. The image then shifts from wasting to fire: *yēqaḏ yᵉqōḏ kîqôḏ ʾēš*, "a burning shall be kindled, like the burning of fire".

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאֵ֔שׁ וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ לְלֶהָבָ֑ה וּבָעֲרָ֗ה וְאָֽכְלָ֛ה שִׁית֥וֹ וּשְׁמִיר֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: And the light of Israel shall become a fire, and his Holy One a flame; and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאֵ֔שׁ וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ לְלֶהָבָ֑ה וּבָעֲרָ֗ה וְאָֽכְלָ֛ה שִׁית֥וֹ וּשְׁמִיר֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

notes.official: *ʾôr-yiśrāʾēl* "the light of Israel" stands in parallel with *qᵉḏôšô* "his Holy One". The line keeps ASV and NRSV typography: "light" lower case, and "Holy One" capitalised as the established epithet (as in "the Holy One of Israel", 10:20). Capitalising "Light" would turn the phrase into a title in English, which the Hebrew does not mark.

paragraphs.text: וּכְב֤וֹד יַעְרוֹ֙ וְכַרְמִלּ֔וֹ מִנֶּ֥פֶשׁ וְעַד־בָּשָׂ֖ר יְכַלֶּ֑ה וְהָיָ֖ה כִּמְסֹ֥ס נֹסֵֽס׃

i18n.en: And the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field he will consume, both soul and body; and it shall be as when a sick man wastes away.
i18n.he: וּכְב֤וֹד יַעְרוֹ֙ וְכַרְמִלּ֔וֹ מִנֶּ֥פֶשׁ וְעַד־בָּשָׂ֖ר יְכַלֶּ֑ה וְהָיָ֖ה כִּמְסֹ֥ס נֹסֵֽס׃

notes.official:
*kimsōs nōsēs* is a hapax pair, and the line follows the modern lexical analysis: "as when a sick man wastes away". *mᵉsōs* is from *māsas* "melt, dissolve", and *nōsēs* is assigned by the lexicons to a root *nss* "be sick, waste away" (BDB; page not verified). NRSV has "as when an invalid wastes away". ASV "as when a standard-bearer fainteth" derives *nōsēs* from *nēs* "banner". That etymology is now rarely followed, and the line no longer uses it.

*minnep̄eš wᵉʿaḏ-bāśār*, literally "from life to flesh", is a merism for the whole, rendered "both soul and body" with ASV and NRSV. The overlay `nefesh-throat-sheol-isaiah-5` (the physical "throat" of 5:14) does not govern this site.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ מִסְפָּ֣ר יִֽהְי֑וּ וְנַ֖עַר יִכְתְּבֵֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child may write them down.
i18n.he: וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ מִסְפָּ֣ר יִֽהְי֑וּ וְנַ֖עַר יִכְתְּבֵֽם׃ (פ)

notes.official: *yiḵtᵉḇēm* "may write them down" uses the verb *kāṯaḇ* of 10:1. The scribes of the woe-oracle write unjust decrees, and here a child could write down the trees that remain. *šᵉʾār* "remnant" begins the chapter's remnant series (10:19–22).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹֽא־יוֹסִ֨יף ע֜וֹד שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלֵיטַ֣ת בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֔ב לְהִשָּׁעֵ֖ן עַל־מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְנִשְׁעַ֗ן עַל־יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and the survivors of the house of Jacob, shall no more again lean on the one who struck them, but shall lean on YHWH, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹֽא־יוֹסִ֨יף ע֜וֹד שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלֵיטַ֣ת בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֔ב לְהִשָּׁעֵ֖ן עַל־מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְנִשְׁעַ֗ן עַל־יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃

notes.official: *pᵉlêṭaṯ bêṯ-yaʿăqōḇ* is rendered "the survivors of the house of Jacob", matching *pᵉlêṭaṯ yiśrāʾēl* "the survivors of Israel" at 4:2. ASV has "they that are escaped". Central `pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus` discusses this verse, but its wohChoice is the event sense "a great deliverance" (Gen 45:7), so it is cited and not extended. *mak-kēhû* "the one who struck them" is Assyria, the rod of 10:5. *bᵉʾĕmeṯ* is "in truth", leaning in faithfulness.

paragraphs.text: שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל־אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
i18n.he: שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל־אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר׃

notes.official:
*šᵉʾār yāšûḇ* is the name of Isaiah's son Shear-jashub (7:3). Here it is a clause, "A remnant will return", under `sign-names-isaiah-7-8`. The verse thus spells out the meaning of the name. *yāšûḇ* (Qal imperfect of *šûḇ*) means both "return" and "turn back, repent", and the following *ʾel-ʾēl gibbôr* "to the Mighty God" gives the direction of the turning.

*ʾēl gibbôr* repeats the throne name of 9:5 (Eng. 9:6), and it is rendered "Mighty God" as there (`el-gibbor-mighty-god-isaiah`). Here the phrase plainly designates YHWH, as in *hāʾēl haggāḏōl haggibbōr* "the great, the mighty God" (Deut 10:17; Jer 32:18). The analyses "God is a warrior" and "mighty hero", which bear on the reading of 9:5, are recorded in that entry.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה עַמְּךָ֤ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּלָּי֥וֹן חָר֖וּץ שׁוֹטֵ֥ף צְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: For though your people Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return; a destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה עַמְּךָ֤ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּלָּי֥וֹן חָר֖וּץ שׁוֹטֵ֥ף צְדָקָֽה׃

notes.official:
*šᵉʾār yāšûḇ bô* "a remnant of them will return" uses the sign-name again (`sign-names-isaiah-7-8`), now restrictively: Israel may be as numerous as "the sand of the sea", but only a remnant will return. The comparison is the patriarchal promise-image (Gen 22:17; 32:13), and *kᵉḥôl hayyām* lacks the "seashore" of the central triad entry, which is cited and not extended. Rom 9:27–28 quotes 10:22–23 from the LXX.

*kiḷḷāyôn ḥārûṣ* is "a destruction is determined" (ASV), and *ḥārûṣ* belongs to the same root as *neḥĕrāṣāh* in 10:23 (central `kalah-venecheratzah-decreed-full-end-cross-corpus`). *šôṭēp̄ ṣᵉḏāqāh* "overflowing with righteousness" keeps *ṣᵉḏāqāh* "righteousness" (ASV, NRSV). Here the term names the just verdict that floods over the land. Some modern versions render it "retribution" or "vindication".

paragraphs.text: כִּ֥י כָלָ֖ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֑ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת עֹשֶׂ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For a full end, and that determined, the Lord YHWH of hosts will make in the midst of all the earth.
i18n.he: כִּ֥י כָלָ֖ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֑ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת עֹשֶׂ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*kālāh wᵉneḥĕrāṣāh* "a full end, and that determined" is a fixed pair, recurring at 28:22 and Dan 9:27 (compare 11:36). The line keeps ASV's wording, which the corpus Daniel already uses at 9:27, and central `kalah-venecheratzah-decreed-full-end-cross-corpus` fixes it across books. *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is "the Lord YHWH of hosts" (`adonai-yhwh-compound-isaiah-25`).

*bᵉqereḇ kol-hāʾāreṣ* is rendered "in the midst of all the earth" (ASV, NRSV) under `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`. A territorial reading, "in the midst of the whole land", is also current, since the decree falls on Israel (10:22). The same phrase follows the same pair at 28:22, which is not yet drafted.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת אַל־תִּירָ֥א עַמִּ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב צִיּ֖וֹן מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט יַכֶּ֔כָּה וּמַטֵּ֥הוּ יִשָּֽׂא־עָלֶ֖יךָ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says the Lord YHWH of hosts: O my people who dwell in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria, though he strikes you with the rod and lifts up his staff against you after the manner of Egypt.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת אַל־תִּירָ֥א עַמִּ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב צִיּ֖וֹן מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט יַכֶּ֔כָּה וּמַטֵּ֥הוּ יִשָּֽׂא־עָלֶ֖יךָ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

notes.official:
*ʾal-tîrāʾ* "do not be afraid" opens a salvation oracle to "my people who dwell in Zion". Central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula` lists this verse, but it governs the fuller formula "do not fear, for I am with you", so it is cited and not extended.

*bᵉḏereḵ miṣrāyim*, here and at 10:26, is rendered "after the manner of Egypt" (ASV; NRSV "as the Egyptians did"). The literal "on the way of Egypt" is possible, and at 10:26 it suggests the route of the Exodus. "Egypt" is printed in English form, as in the signed-off Isaiah chapters.

paragraphs.text: כִּי־ע֖וֹד מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֑ר וְכָ֣לָה זַ֔עַם וְאַפִּ֖י עַל־תַּבְלִיתָֽם׃

i18n.en: For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall come to an end, and my anger shall be directed to their destruction.
i18n.he: כִּי־ע֖וֹד מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֑ר וְכָ֣לָה זַ֔עַם וְאַפִּ֖י עַל־תַּבְלִיתָֽם׃

notes.official: *taḇlîṯām* is a hapax, "their wearing out, destruction". The line supplies "directed" with ASV and keeps the Masoretic plural "their", where ASV has "his". An emendation, *ʿal-tēḇēl yittōm* ("my anger against the world will come to an end"), is reported in the commentaries. It is not MT and is not adopted (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *zaʿam* "indignation" is the word of 10:5.

paragraphs.text: וְעוֹרֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שׁ֔וֹט כְּמַכַּ֥ת מִדְיָ֖ן בְּצ֣וּר עוֹרֵ֑ב וּמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ עַל־הַיָּ֔ם וּנְשָׂא֖וֹ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And YHWH of hosts will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and his staff shall be over the sea, and he will lift it up after the manner of Egypt.
i18n.he: וְעוֹרֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שׁ֔וֹט כְּמַכַּ֥ת מִדְיָ֖ן בְּצ֣וּר עוֹרֵ֑ב וּמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ עַל־הַיָּ֔ם וּנְשָׂא֖וֹ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

notes.official: Two precedents are recalled. *makkaṯ midyān bᵉṣûr ʿôrēḇ* is the defeat of Midian at the rock of Oreb (Judg 7:25; compare 9:3 "as on the day of Midian"). *maṭṭēhû ʿal-hayyām* "his staff over the sea" is the staff stretched over the sea at the Exodus (Exod 14:16). *šôṭ* is "a scourge", and the staff is YHWH's own, answering Assyria's staff of 10:24.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָס֤וּר סֻבֳּלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל שִׁכְמֶ֔ךָ וְעֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֑ךָ וְחֻבַּ֥ל עֹ֖ל מִפְּנֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that his burden shall depart from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed by reason of fatness.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָס֤וּר סֻבֳּלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל שִׁכְמֶ֔ךָ וְעֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֑ךָ וְחֻבַּ֥ל עֹ֖ל מִפְּנֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃

notes.official:
*wᵉḥubbal ʿōl mippᵉnê-šāmen* is the chapter's best-known crux. The Masoretic Text reads "and the yoke shall be destroyed by reason of fatness" (ASV), usually explained as the yoke bursting because the ox's neck has grown fat. KJV renders *šemen* as "the anointing", and a messianic reading of the phrase is attested in the Targum (reported in the commentaries; not verified here). NRSV follows an emendation that joins the last words to 10:28 and reads a place name, "He has gone up from Rimmon"; others conjecture "from Samaria" or "from Jeshimon".

The line translates MT and keeps the MT verse division (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *šemen* is "fatness", its sense in the vegetable and animal imagery of the context. "Anointing" would put a cultic reading into the English that the noun here does not require.

paragraphs.text: בָּ֥א עַל־עַיַּ֖ת עָבַ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן לְמִכְמָ֖שׂ יַפְקִ֥יד כֵּלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: He has come to Aiath, he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he lays up his baggage.
i18n.he: בָּ֥א עַל־עַיַּ֖ת עָבַ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן לְמִכְמָ֖שׂ יַפְקִ֥יד כֵּלָֽיו׃

notes.official:
10:28–32 is an itinerary of an army advancing on Jerusalem from the north. Perfects mark the stages already passed, and imperfects the halts (10:28b, 32). Its historical occasion is debated: an Assyrian advance (often tied to 701 BCE), the Syro-Ephraimite march of about 734 BCE, or a literary itinerary. The line identifies no army beyond the "he" of the Hebrew.

*ʿayyaṯ* "Aiath" is generally identified with Ai (Josh 7–8; compare *ʿayyāʾ*, Neh 11:31). A Migron is named near Gibeah at 1 Sam 14:2; whether it is the same site is uncertain. At Michmash the army leaves its baggage (*yap̄qîḏ kēlāyw* "he deposits his equipment") before the steep crossing. Names take their ASV spellings under `march-itinerary-toponyms-isaiah-10`.

paragraphs.text: עָֽבְרוּ֙ מַעְבָּרָ֔ה גֶּ֖בַע מָל֣וֹן לָ֑נוּ חָֽרְדָה֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל נָֽסָה׃

i18n.en: They have gone over the pass; they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
i18n.he: עָֽבְרוּ֙ מַעְבָּרָ֔ה גֶּ֖בַע מָל֣וֹן לָ֑נוּ חָֽרְדָה֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל נָֽסָה׃

notes.official:
*ʿāḇᵉrû maʿbārāh* "they have gone over the pass" refers to the defile of Michmash (*maʿăḇar mikmāś*, 1 Sam 13:23; 14:4). *geḇaʿ mālôn lānû* can be read two ways. As quoted speech, *lānû* means "for us": NJPS "Geba is to be our night quarters!". As narrative, it is the verb *lānû* "they lodged" (from *lyn/lûn*). The accentuation does not decide between them, since the suffixed preposition is also stressed on the first syllable (compare 9:5; 1:9). The line keeps the narrative reading of ASV and JPS 1917, "they have taken up their lodging at Geba"; NRSV reads the same way ("at Geba they lodge for the night", from memory, not verified).

Ramah trembles and "Gibeah of Saul" (Saul's town, 1 Sam 10:26; 11:4) has fled: the verbs register the panic of each town as the army passes.

paragraphs.text: צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת־גַּלִּ֑ים הַקְשִׁ֥יבִי לַ֖יְשָׁה עֲנִיָּ֥ה עֲנָתֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Cry aloud with your voice, O daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O poor Anathoth!
i18n.he: צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת־גַּלִּ֑ים הַקְשִׁ֥יבִי לַ֖יְשָׁה עֲנִיָּ֥ה עֲנָתֽוֹת׃

notes.official:
Three towns are addressed. *baṯ-gallîm* "O daughter of Gallim" personifies the town, as "the daughter of Zion" (1:8). Gallim is the home of Palti (1 Sam 25:44). *layᵉšāh* "Laishah" may be a town of that name, or Laish with directional *-āh*. The name is kept as written.

*ʿăniyyāh ʿănāṯôṯ* is "O poor Anathoth!" in the Masoretic Text (ASV), with a sound-play on the name. Anathoth is the priestly town of Jer 1:1. A repointing *ʿănîhā* "answer her, O Anathoth!" (NRSV) keeps the run of imperatives and is favoured by many commentators. The line translates MT (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: נָדְדָ֖ה מַדְמֵנָ֑ה יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַגֵּבִ֖ים הֵעִֽיזוּ׃

i18n.en: Madmenah is in flight; the inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.
i18n.he: נָדְדָ֖ה מַדְמֵנָ֑ה יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַגֵּבִ֖ים הֵעִֽיזוּ׃

notes.official: Madmenah is a town on the northern approach. It is unrelated to the *madmēnāh* "dung-pit" of 25:10, whose ketiv/qere entry is not applied here. Gebim is otherwise unknown. *hēʿîzû* "flee for safety" is the Hiphil of *ʿwz* "take refuge, bring to safety" (ASV "flee to save themselves").

paragraphs.text: ע֥וֹד הַיּ֖וֹם בְּנֹ֣ב לַֽעֲמֹ֑ד יְנֹפֵ֤ף יָדוֹ֙ הַ֣ר בית־[בַּת־] צִיּ֔וֹן גִּבְעַ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: This very day he shall halt at Nob; he shakes his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
i18n.he: ע֥וֹד הַיּ֖וֹם בְּנֹ֣ב לַֽעֲמֹ֑ד יְנֹפֵ֤ף יָדוֹ֙ הַ֣ר בית־[בַּת־] צִיּ֔וֹן גִּבְעַ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*ʿôḏ hayyôm bᵉnōḇ laʿămōḏ* is literally "yet today at Nob to stand", and ASV's "This very day he shall halt at Nob" is kept. Nob is the priestly town of 1 Sam 21–22, within sight of Jerusalem. The gesture *yᵉnōp̄ēp̄ yāḏô* "he shakes his hand" ends the march at the city's edge.

The ketiv reads בית *bêṯ* ("the mountain of the house of Zion") and the qere בַּת *baṯ* ("the mount of the daughter of Zion"). The qere is translated (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`), matching "the daughter of Zion" at 1:8.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְסָעֵ֥ף פֻּארָ֖ה בְּמַעֲרָצָ֑ה וְרָמֵ֤י הַקּוֹמָה֙ גְּדוּעִ֔ים וְהַגְּבֹהִ֖ים יִשְׁפָּֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: Behold, the Sovereign, YHWH of hosts, will lop the boughs with terror; and the high of stature shall be hewn down, and the lofty shall be brought low.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְסָעֵ֥ף פֻּארָ֖ה בְּמַעֲרָצָ֑ה וְרָמֵ֤י הַקּוֹמָה֙ גְּדוּעִ֔ים וְהַגְּבֹהִ֖ים יִשְׁפָּֽלוּ׃

notes.official: *hā-ʾāḏôn YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is rendered "the Sovereign, YHWH of hosts" as at 10:16 (provisional; `ha-adon-articular-title-isaiah`, founder ruling pending). After the march of 10:28–32 the image turns to a forester felling trees. *mᵉsāʿēp̄ puʾrāh* is "will lop the boughs", and *bᵉmaʿărāṣāh* "with terror" (ASV) is from the root *ʿrṣ* "terrify". NRSV has "with terrifying power", and an "axe" sense has been proposed from context. The tall trees stand for the proud, as in 2:12–17.

paragraphs.text: וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.
i18n.he: וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל׃ (ס)

notes.official: *wᵉhallᵉḇānôn bᵉʾaddîr yippôl* is rendered "and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one" (ASV), with *ʾaddîr* as agent. The agent is left unspecified, as in the Hebrew; commentators refer it to YHWH or to Assyria's destroyer. NRSV reads *ʾaddîr* of the trees themselves, "Lebanon with its majestic trees will fall". The forest image of 10:33–34 leads directly into the shoot from the stump of Jesse at 11:1.
